title: Evaluation & production RAG
summary: The last module turns the pieces into a system you can run, trust and improve: **synthetic evaluation data** written from the documents, **retrieval and answer metrics** (including LLM judges and LangSmith's evaluate, run locally), **security** (injected documents, access control, personal data), and **performance**. The capstone measures the complete Nimbus RAG system (everything built in Modules 1–9) against its first version on hand-labelled, synthetic and unanswerable questions.
learn: **Synthetic evaluation data**: questions written from chunks, filtered, saved and reused
**Evaluating retrieval**: hit rate and MRR on two sets, setups side by side, decisions from numbers
**Evaluating answers**: faithfulness, relevance, correctness and context precision, by a judge model; LangSmith evaluate()
**RAG security**: indirect prompt injection, access control at retrieval time, redacting personal data
**Performance and cost**: where the time goes, tokens per k, concurrency, streaming
**The capstone**: the complete system, measured against v1
flow:
INGEST   files → loaders v3 (+OCR) → registry (dates, access) → clean → chunk 300/50 + headers → security scan
         (quarantine injections, redact personal data) → bge-small → pgvector (HNSW + full-text index, record manager)
ANSWER   question (+history) → rewrite → translate if non-ASCII → hybrid search (valid today, this audience may read)
         → FlashRank → numbered sources → grounded structured answer → verified citations
         (or the knowledge agent: documents + read-only SQL)
MEASURE  45 hand-labelled + synthetic + unanswerable questions → retrieval metrics + judged answer metrics

labs.explain:
Write questions **from** chunks (each chunk is the known right answer), keep only those whose quote is really in the chunk, that don't copy its words and that a critic finds specific, and **save** the set so every evaluation uses the same questions. Then compare two retrievers on it.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: The quote must be in the chunk.
A question made of the chunk's own words is a lookup.
The critic's question: specific and self-contained; company-specific is fine.

labs.explain:
Four retrieval setups (vector, hybrid, each with and without the reranker) on the hand-labelled and the synthetic sets: hit@k, MRR and latency side by side, and the reranker's price against its gain.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Answers judged on four axes in **one call** by a **different model** (Groq) than the one answering (Mistral): faithfulness, relevance, correctness against a reference, and context precision. The same run goes through **LangSmith's evaluate()** locally, with a code evaluator (was the expected source retrieved?) and a judge evaluator.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: Judges sometimes return invalid JSON (three times in a row, in this module's first capstone run): retry, then fall back to tool calling, then to the next judge model.
Share of claims the sources support.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

Where one answer's time goes (retrieval vs generation), how context tokens grow with k, sequential vs concurrent model calls, and **streaming** with the sources shown first.

path.title: Capstone: the complete Nimbus RAG system
path.summary: Everything from Modules 1–9 as one production system: loaders for every format with OCR, a document registry (validity dates, access levels), structure-aware chunking with headers, ingestion-time security, hybrid search with reranking, translation for non-English questions, grounded answers with verified citations, a knowledge agent for structured data, and a measurement harness. The capstone evaluation runs it against v1 on hand-labelled, synthetic and unanswerable questions, judged by another model.

steps.title: Ingest
steps.explain: `nimbus rag ingest`: loaders v3 (OCR for scans and images), registry facts on every Document, cleaning, chunking v2, then the security pass: chunks that address the model are quarantined (listed in the report, never indexed) and personal emails and phone numbers are redacted before embedding. The record manager keeps the index in sync.

notes.text: Security runs on every chunk before embedding.

production: Review the quarantine list: rules have false positives (a security policy quoting an attack phrase).
Rules catch known phrasings only; add a classifier for anything user-supplied (uploads, tickets).

steps.title: Retrieve
steps.tagline: Who may read what, as of when
steps.explain: The Retriever translates non-English questions, runs hybrid search among documents valid on the date AND readable by the audience (`public` for customers, `staff` for employees; anything not marked public is staff-only), and reranks. Access control happens inside the search, so a customer's answer can't be built from staff documents.

notes.text: Only documents marked public are public.

production: The audience must come from the authenticated session, never from the question or the client (the FastAPI track wires this to API keys).
Test access control like a feature: a public question about a staff topic must answer 'I don't know'.

steps.title: Answer
steps.explain: `nimbus rag ask "…" --audience public|staff`: the Answerer (Module 7) with the sources-are-data rule, verified citations and refusals; the knowledge agent (Module 8) for questions over the menu and orders.
production: Stream the answer with sources first (lab 5) in the API: perceived latency is time to first token.

steps.title: Measure
steps.explain: `nimbus rag synth` writes the synthetic set (17 questions kept of 26 written, after the evidence, copy and critic filters). `nimbus rag eval` scores retrieval; the capstone lab adds judged answer metrics.
production: Re-run on every change to loaders, chunking, retrieval, prompts or model, and keep the history: regressions show up as a drop, not a complaint.
Spot-check a sample of judge verdicts by hand each release.

steps.title: Capstone
steps.tagline: The production answerer vs a naive baseline
steps.explain:
Both systems search today's index (loaders v3, OCR, chunking v2: those gains were measured in their modules: answerable 0.64 → 1.00, hit@5 0.56 → 0.93). The capstone compares how questions are answered: 12 synthetic, 12 hand-labelled (spread across all sources) and 6 unanswerable questions, judged by Groq's gpt-oss-20b. The production answerer is more often correct and faithful, refuses every unanswerable question (the baseline answered 4 of them), at 1.3× the tokens and a lower median latency.

| | correct | faithfulness | relevance | refused the unanswerable | tokens / question | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline: dense search + naive prompt | 0.92 | 0.94 | 0.92 | 2/6 | 472 | 2.6 s |
| **v1.0: the production answerer** | 0.96 | 0.99 | 0.96 | 6/6 | 636 | 2.1 s |
production: What's next lives in the other tracks: LangGraph agents with memory and human approval, MCP servers, the FastAPI service, and production operations (caching, tracing, deployment).
